reason: The cited evidence supports that laser cladding produces high-quality coatings (E2, E4) and that WC-reinforced AlCoCrFeNi HEA coatings improve hardness and wear resistance (E4). However, no cited passage provides evidence that HEA coatings mitigate hot cracking compared to fusion welding, which is a key premise of the hypothesis.
premises: Laser cladding can produce dense, metallurgically bonded coatings with low dilution and minimal defects
AlCoCrFeNi-based HEAs can improve hardness and wear resistance when deposited as a coating
Adding WC particles to an HEA matrix further enhances hardness and wear resistance
HEA coatings can mitigate hot cracking relative to traditional fusion welding
